subject: SLA exception triage & cost attribution workbench request
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SLA exception triage + a lightweight Route Attribution Workbench (initial ask)

Folks —

Quick ask coming out of a support escalation with AuriCloud (details below): they saw a spike in tail latency and an associated cost bump over a 48hr window. CS put a problem statement to me: they need a way to quickly answer "which endpoints, models, or config changes (quantization/cache/batching) drove the spike" and tie that to dollar impact.

What I want to propose as a minimal ship: a small "Route Attribution Workbench" inside Console that lets operators and CS: 
- filter by time window & region
- see per-route token spend and p50/p95/p99 latencies side-by-side
- break down cost by model variant, batching profile, and cache hit
- flag SLO-exception windows and surface likely root-cause candidates (e.g., model variant fallback, cache miss surge)

Why now: AuriCloud is willing to pilot if we can give them an exploratory view + the ability to export the list of affected tenants and approximate cost delta. This would also be useful internally for SREs when a canary or autoscale misbehaves.

Ask: can product + eng + design scope a small POC (console page + two backend queries) that we can demo to AuriCloud in 2 weeks? I attached a tiny log sample and a very rough mock.

Attachments: slo-exception-log-sample.csv, route-attribution-mockup-v1.png

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception triage + a lightweight Route Attribution Workbench (initial ask)

Nice summary, Vivek — good call to push a compact first release. A couple of quick questions from the product side:

1) Primary user: is this for CS/SRE first (read-only) or also for product/engineering to run ad-hoc queries? I want to get permissions/roles right.
2) Export format: AuriCloud asked for "tenant-level monthly delta" — do we need to compute that in the workbench or is a CSV export of per-route per-tenant totals OK?
3) Acceptance criteria for pilot: what constitutes "demoable" to AuriCloud? A 10–15m walkthrough showing identify -> export -> ticket?

I agree: target POC in 2 weeks is aggressive but feasible if eng accepts a narrow telemetry surface. Markus — can you confirm if we currently have the telemetry to break out cost by model variant + cache hit for a historical 48h window?

I'll start a short product spec after we confirm the telemetry and roles.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception triage + a lightweight Route Attribution Workbench (initial ask)

Short answer: we can do a focused POC in two weeks if we constrain scope. Current state of telemetry:
- We have per-request metadata with route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, and timestamps persisted in ClickHouse for 90 days.
- Cache hit/miss is logged but at a sampling rate (1 in 10). We can surface sampled cache-hit proportions, but absolute counts will require increasing sampling or reconstructing via KV cache metrics.
- Batching profile is derivable from runtime logs, but not currently joined to per-request rows — that will need a small ETL (1-day job) to attach batching buckets.

Engineering asks for the POC:
- Narrow initial time window to 7d and default to 48h (as Vivek suggested)
- Limit UI to: time filter + route selector + table with columns [route, model_variant, tokens, p50/p95/p99, estimated_cost, cache_hit_rate_sampled]
- Backend: two aggregated queries (latency + token/cost by grouping) and a join to sampled cache hits
- Export: CSV with per-tenant totals and an estimated cost delta column computed with current price profiles

Risks: cost-estimate accuracy will be +/- 10–20% initially because of sampling and batching attribution. We should call that out in the UI.

I can commit Eng resources for the POC if Product narrows the acceptance criteria. Happy to sync with Laura and Marissa on Monday.

—Markus
Lead Backend Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Carolyn Li <carolyn@auricloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: AuriCloud Platform <platform@auricloud.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception triage + a lightweight Route Attribution Workbench (initial ask)

Thanks Vivek/Laura — AuriCloud is happy to be the pilot. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tenant-level export is ideal; monthly deltas are the metric our finance team wants to see (we can compute monthly from exported timestamps).
- We need the UI to allow us to select multiple tenants and tag them as "impact" so we can prioritize outreach.
- Willing to share more logs if that helps with cache-hit reconstruction — happy to provide a 7-day trace.

If it helps, we can have a short 30m sync with your team this week to walk through the exact fields we need in the CSV.

—Carolyn
Carolyn Li
Head of Platform Engineering, AuriCloud

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Carolyn Li <carolyn@auricloud.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception triage + a lightweight Route Attribution Workbench (initial ask) — next steps

Thanks all — quick summary and owners: 

1) Scope (POC): 48h default window, UI with filter + single-route table, CSV export with per-tenant totals and estimated_cost_delta column. Call out +/- 10–20% accuracy for cost. (Product to write short spec) — Owner: Laura (due: Mon 12/21).
2) Telemetry & Backend: two aggregated queries + sampling join for cache hit; small ETL to attach batching buckets if feasible. (Eng to validate infra & commits) — Owner: Markus (due: Thu 12/17).
3) Design: produce a single compact mock for the POC (PNG attached) and a short copy doc for the accuracy caveat. — Owner: Marissa (due: Fri 12/18).
4) CS/Pilot coordination: Monica to schedule the 30m sync with AuriCloud this week and collect the 7-day trace if needed. — Owner: Monica (due: Wed 12/16).

If everyone is aligned I'll open a concise JIRA (SUP-3249) to track the POC tasks and we will use the pilot to decide whether this becomes a Console feature.

One more ask: Markus, please include one example query in the PR that demonstrates the cost delta calc logic (so Product can validate numbers).

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
